title: Retention controls + compliance reporting pack (v1)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
## Summary
Enterprise prospects are consistently asking for (a) tenant-configurable retention controls and (b) a standard “compliance pack” we can hand over during security/procurement reviews. Today we have a mix of fixed retentions across stores plus ad-hoc explanations, which increases sales friction and creates audit/evidence gaps.

This initiative delivers:
1) **Tenant-configurable retention controls (v1)** across key datasets (audit logs, admin activity, inference request metadata, telemetry/analytics, selected operational logs where applicable).
2) A baseline **compliance reporting pack (v1)** suitable for customer security reviews and internal SOC 2/ISO-aligned evidence collection.

## Goals (v1)
### Product goals
- Provide retention settings per tenant with **safe defaults** and **clear guardrails** (min/max, no “never delete” unless explicitly permitted, legal hold override).
- Make retention posture **easy to explain and demonstrate** in Console and via exportable evidence.
- Support Hosted + Dedicated first; Private where feasible with clear documentation of differences.

### Engineering goals (what “done” looks like)
- Retention policies are **enforceable** (TTL/compaction/scheduled deletion jobs as appropriate) and **auditable** (who changed what, when; last enforcement run; exceptions/holds).
- Deterministic “effective policy” calculation with precedence rules (org/tenant/env/region) and test coverage.
- Observability around enforcement jobs (lag, errors, delete throughput, bloat risk).

### Compliance goals
- Standardized pack includes control-to-evidence mapping + repeatable evidence collection procedure.
- Pack can be generated for a tenant/time window and shared by Sales/SE with minimal bespoke work.

## Non-goals / out of scope (for v1)
- Full custom retention across every infra log stream (some remain governed by SRE standards and vendor limits).
- Customer-configurable retention for all raw inference payload content (requires broader data handling decisions).
- Long-term archival / WORM storage as a product feature (can be revisited for regulated verticals).

## Primary user stories
1) As a tenant admin, I can set retention durations for supported data types (within allowed bounds) and see the effective policy.
2) As a security reviewer, I can understand what data is retained for how long, and see evidence that deletion is enforced.
3) As Support/SRE, I can verify enforcement is running and respond to failures without risking accidental over-deletion.
4) As Legal/Compliance, I can place a **legal hold** to pause deletion for specific tenant(s)/dataset(s) and track approvals.

## Scope (v1) — datasets & policy surface
Initial supported datasets (final list to be confirmed in Discovery):
- Audit logs (admin + security relevant events)
- Admin activity logs (Console + API configuration changes)
- Inference request metadata (non-payload metadata: timestamps, model id, token counts, status codes)
- Telemetry/analytics tables eligible for tenant retention (aggregated usage tables where tenant-scoped)
- Selected operational logs where tenant-scoped and technically feasible

Policy attributes (v1):
- Retention duration (days)
- Region/environment applicability (Hosted/Dedicated/Private as applicable)
- Legal hold override (on/off) and exception workflow reference
- Guardrails: min/max per dataset; prevent invalid combinations; defaults by tier

## Milestones & timeline (target 10–12 weeks)
### Phase 1: Discovery & requirements (Weeks 1–2)
- Complete data inventory + identify eligible datasets by store (owners + enforcement option)
- Confirm required defaults/guardrails by tier (Hosted self-serve vs Enterprise)
- Agree on v1 compliance pack outline + target artifacts

### Phase 2: Design (Weeks 2–4)
- Retention policy schema + precedence rules (ADR + examples)
- Enforcement approach per datastore (TTL vs job vs hybrid)
- Console IA + wireframes + copy for edge cases (holds/exceptions)
- Evidence strategy (what we can prove and how we’ll snapshot it)

### Phase 3: Implementation (Weeks 4–9)
- Control plane: policy persistence + validation
- Policy evaluation library: effective policy computation + golden tests
- Enforcement worker(s) for audit log store and selected analytics stores
- Console: settings page + effective policy view + enforcement status panel
- Auditability: emit audit events for policy changes; show change history

### Phase 4: Reporting pack + validation (Weeks 7–10)
- Control mapping and evidence collection runbook
- Draft customer-facing pack + internal version
- Trial run: generate pack for an internal sandbox tenant + one friendly design partner

### Phase 5: Rollout (Weeks 9–12)
- Feature flag + staged rollout (internal → canary enterprise tenants → broader enterprise)
- Monitoring and on-call readiness for enforcement jobs
- Sales enablement + Support playbooks + docs

## Success metrics
### Product / GTM
- Reduce time-to-close friction: “Retention controls” section in security questionnaire requires <2 follow-ups on average (tracked by SE notes + Support tags).
- 80%+ of enterprise security reviews accept the v1 compliance pack without requesting a custom retention memo.
- At least 3 enterprise deals in Q2 cite retention controls / compliance pack as “unblocked.”

### Engineering / reliability
- Enforcement jobs meet SLO: 99% of eligible partitions/records deleted within policy window + 24h grace (excluding legal holds).
- No P0/P1 incidents caused by retention enforcement load after rollout (or a documented mitigation plan if we hit limits).
- Console shows accurate effective policy and last-run status for 99% of requests.

### Compliance
- Evidence collection runbook can be executed by GRC in <2 hours end-to-end for a standard reporting period.
- Control-to-evidence mapping is complete and reviewed/approved by GRC + Security Eng.

## Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag: `retention_controls_v1` (per-tenant enablement).
- Stages:
  1) Internal tenants + dogfood (1 week)
  2) Canary: 2–3 enterprise tenants with explicit comms + rollback plan
  3) General availability for Enterprise tiers (Hosted + Dedicated)
  4) Private deployments: documented availability by version; coordinate with release/upgrade cadence
- Backwards compatibility: existing tenants retain current behavior until they opt into v1 (or until default migration is approved).
- Change management:
  - Emit audit events on policy changes
  - “Dry-run” mode for enforcement in canary (log-only) for first 48h where feasible
  - Rate limits/safety caps in deletion workers; SRE alerts on load anomalies

- ENG-2926 — Console backend endpoints for retention settings

- ENG-2940 — Compliance reporting pack generator
- ENG-2944 — Observability dashboards/alerts for enforcement

## Risks & mitigations
- **Datastore load/impact:** Deletion jobs can cause elevated DB load.
  - Mitigation: batching, rate limits, off-peak scheduling, SRE alerts, and kill switch per worker.
- **Ambiguous dataset boundaries:** “Telemetry” includes mixed tenant-scoped and platform-scoped tables.
  - Mitigation: explicitly list eligible tables in v1, document non-eligible categories.
- **Customer expectation mismatch (e.g., “never delete”):**
  - Mitigation: firm guardrails + clear docs; exceptions only through legal hold workflow.
- **Private deployment variability:**
  - Mitigation: define supported matrix; document what is configurable in Private and what remains operator-managed.

## Open questions
1) Default retention values by tier (proposed): Audit logs 365d (Enterprise), 90d (Standard), 30d (Free); admin activity aligned with audit logs.
2) Legal hold semantics: global per tenant vs per dataset; approval workflow requirements (Legal vs Security vs GRC).
3) What evidence is acceptable for “deletion enforced” (screenshots + job logs + metrics vs immutable reports).
4) For inference request metadata: confirm which fields are retained and whether any are considered sensitive in certain regulated verticals.
